text: The last six are special cases, a sentence or two each. A degenerate dimension is a dimension with no table behind it, like an invoice number kept on the fact. You still group by it. A junk dimension gathers small flags, payment type, gift or not, web or store, into one table of every combination: twelve rows, and the fact carries one key instead of three. A role-playing dimension is one table in several roles: the date dimension, joined once as the order date and once as the ship date. A mini-dimension moves fast-changing attributes, like age band and income tier, out of a big customer dimension into a small one, twenty rows here, with its own key on the fact. The big one stops growing a new version every time a band changes. A factless fact table has no measures at all: one row per event, like a student attending a class. Counting the rows is the measure. And a surrogate key from a sequence is a small integer, handed out in order: compact and quick to join. The other choice is a UUID, a universally unique identifier: sixteen bytes any system can make without a shared counter, which matters when many sources insert at once. The cost shows in the index. In Postgres, a hundred thousand random UUIDs built a primary key index almost twice the size of the sequence's. Time-ordered version seven UUIDs land in between. Every table here is filled by a load job: close a version, insert a placeholder, split a weight. Loading the model takes code. Next: Python for data engineering.
